PullRequest.Title: Andysalerno/fusion staged streaming
PullRequest.Body:

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new handler passes the unique phase tool-call ID into _emitReasoningDelta/_emitMarkdownDelta. CopilotReasoningTiming explicitly accumulates their content in its session-owned _scopes map. Traced abort, error, phase-chat closure, and turn-reset paths do not clear these phase keys; only real subagent completion clears a child scope. Static evidence establishes retention; cancellation frequency and output size determine its magnitude.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Accumulated reasoning and markdown strings, response-part objects, and timing scopes in CopilotReasoningTiming._scopes.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained bytes grow with the sum of streamed output prefixes across cancelled child-chat phases with distinct Fusion IDs in the same live session; there is no eviction or per-phase content cap.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Session-long retained heap growth and additional GC pressure after repeatedly stopping long repair/revision generations.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the phase's first complete assistant.message, provisional text/reasoning deltas were handled in the root timing scope. That scope was cleared when the root turn ended or the next turn started, rather than retaining interrupted output under a unique phase ID.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Repair/revision deltas now accumulate under fusion:<fusionId>:<phaseId>. Cancelling before the complete message prevents completeMessage from releasing scope.parts, but the phase cleanup only removes routing state, leaving the accumulated strings reachable for the session lifetime.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 12572–12578 route provisional deltas into phase-keyed timing scopes. Previously these deltas used the ordinary root handlers at 11705/13466, whose undefined-key scope is cleared on the next _startTurn (3936). Consider cancellation before the phase's first complete assistant.message: before this change no partial model output was accumulated under that phase key.
Findings.Title: Clear phase timing scopes when a staged stream is cancelled
Findings.Impact: Stopping a repair or revision while it streams, before its first complete assistant.message, leaves an extra retained copy of its partial output even after subsequent turns. Repeated cancellations in a long-lived chat accumulate these copies until the CopilotAgentSession is disposed.
Findings.Evidence: CopilotReasoningTiming.start/getScope stores each phase in _scopes (copilotReasoningTiming.ts:63–68,160–165), and append/markdown retain concatenated content (71–94). completeMessage normally empties scope.parts (132–138), but late provisional messages are rejected by _fusionPhaseToolCallId after cancellation (copilotAgentSession.ts:3257–3258). _forgetFusionPhaseChats (14636–14640) and _completeFusionPhaseChats (14642–14675) never clear timing scopes; _startTurn clears only undefined (3936). _clearSubagentResponseParts does clear a child key (3903–3906), but its sole caller is the real-subagent completion path (3381–3385), not Fusion phase closure.
Findings.Recommendation: Clear each phase-owned timing scope when its chat is definitively cancelled or closed, respecting the existing drain/reopen ordering. Include the abort/forget path, not just normal message completion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Inline Fusion draft/main-pass output and critic/judge review output
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SDK callbacks synchronously classify events and update response state. Inline reasoning is displayed as deltas; inline answers still wait for commit, and review output waits for phase completion. No new model execution, tool execution, or awaited service read is added by these handlers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish chat response-part/reasoning/delta actions through the existing action protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical progress action per accepted reasoning delta, plus part/timing lifecycle actions. Before the PR the ordinary handlers already forwarded provisional deltas to the root; the new filter removes inline text and review deltas from that path. Transport framing does not determine the finding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provisional stream events reached the ordinary root handlers. The PR routes them explicitly and suppresses streams that must wait for commit/review completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local state updates occur in the callback; renderer delivery is asynchronous. No response waits for a new remote round trip.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of text/reasoning deltas and complete messages per model call; typically a small number of workflow phases, each potentially producing long output.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event handlers run synchronously. Existing progress publication can queue behind a pending tool completion per parent tool-call key; there is no newly introduced parallel operation per delta.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-phase stream flags allocate once on the first accepted delta, are removed at the last complete message, and are cleared with provisional state on turn reset/completion. Reasoning deduplication remains turn-owned. Review and inline-text deltas are rejected before stream-state allocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: wrapper filtering, provisional dispatch, ordinary stream handlers, and shared emitters were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual delta frequency and protocol frame batching are not measured; no added fan-out or repeated whole-output processing was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression on the normal inline/review path. Streaming is rerouted rather than blindly added alongside the ordinary handler.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live repair/revision phase-chat streaming and successful message completion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first accepted delta opens the phase chat synchronously; subsequent deltas reuse it. Complete provisional messages suppress already-streamed text/reasoning. Catalog persistence and response-layout persistence are fire-and-forget rather than prerequisites for displaying progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register and persist the private phase chat and its storage identity/catalog metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One startup/persistence sequence per opened phase, with the existing reopen lifecycle; not per delta. The first delta can now precede the complete message that previously opened it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same chat-creation/persistence sequence was reached by complete provisional messages or tools; the diff moves its first occurrence to the first streamed output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registration is synchronous, while the catalog persistence promise is not awaited by stream rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize recorded reasoning/markdown layout and upsert it into the session database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Successful layout recording is at complete-message boundaries, not delta boundaries: one persist, with a possible timing-finalization update if reasoning was still active. Each persist performs two SQL statements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The persistence facility already existed for ordinary streamed reasoning. Phase output was supplied as complete chunks; observing its reasoning and markdown in one phase scope can newly make phase layouts eligible for recording.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The callback launches persistence without awaiting it; it does not block the next delta or model call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Route output actions to the phase chat instead of the root chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical action per accepted delta, plus chat lifecycle actions. Ordinary typed listeners reject the same provisional events, so the wrapper does not double-dispatch them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Deltas were forwarded by ordinary root listeners while complete provisional messages were separately rendered in the phase chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Uses existing progress/action delivery; no awaited IPC request is added.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Accepted delta count and total output bytes across child-chat phases/model calls. Chat creation is deduplicated per open phase, not repeated per delta.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: In-process stream handling is sequential. _fusionPhaseChats coalesces chat startup; existing per-key progress sequencing preserves pending tool-result ordering. Private-chat persistence is enqueued per session, not launched once per token.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold phase: first delta creates stream flags and opens the chat. Warm phase: map/set lookups reuse the chat and response parts. The complete-message path consumes the flags and existing message/reasoning sets suppress committed duplicates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: startup set guard, duplicate suppression, database callback, SQL implementation, and per-session catalog queue were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No throughput measurements; successful-stream persistence size depends on output length. Its bounded message-level cadence does not establish a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: Normal successful streaming has no separately reportable performance issue. Interrupted-stream ownership is covered by the finding below.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancel a streaming repair/revision before its first complete message, then continue using the same session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cancellation sets the late-event gate, aborts the SDK execution, forgets phase routing, and allows later turns. Retained timing scopes are not on the cancellation latency path but remain reachable afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing session.abort call per cancellation, independent of streamed byte count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same abort request existed. Partial provisional stream content was accumulated in the root timing scope, which was cleared on reuse rather than stranded under a phase key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: abort awaits the SDK request; the memory regression persists after this settles and after later turns start.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Sum of partial reasoning/markdown output bytes across interrupted child-chat phases with distinct fusion/phase keys over the live session lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One retained scope per affected phase key; repeated cancellations accumulate even with completely sequential turns. This is not a concurrency-burst issue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The stream-flag map is cleared, but it does not own the accumulated output. CopilotReasoningTiming._scopes retains each phase's partial parts. Turn startup clears only the undefined/root scope; real-subagent completion clears child scopes but Fusion close/forget does not. Disposal eventually clears all scopes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all timing-scope clear sites, abort/idle/error paths, phase close/forget paths, and subsequent-turn reset were traced. Existing tests explicitly exercise cancellation followed by reuse of the same session.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of user cancellations and partial-output lengths are unknown. These affect severity, not the established lifetime/scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity cleanup-lifecycle regression at copilotAgentSession.ts:12575: newly phase-keyed partial streams retain output until session disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Microsoft account selection, conversation creation/resume, and setup restoration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Conversation launch awaits account login and active-account confirmation before finalization. getActive replaces the old activeAccount query at the same confirmation point; account-kind renames do not add another enumeration or login.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the active account with session.rpc.accounts.getActive().
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per active-account verification, replacing one accounts.get({query:{kind:'activeAccount'}}) RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One targeted active-account RPC with the old API shape; no full-list read was present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited during the same authentication confirmation stage as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the setup/conversation session, advance/select/cancel login, and disconnect/delete rejected or released sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing flow-dependent begin/advance/cancel operations per login; at most one explicit selection advance for the selected service. Shared setup creation is amortized across warm conversation launches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical state machine and call placement; the diff updates account-kind names and the single verification RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Launch/login operations are awaited; cleanup retains its existing ownership and ordering. Any runtime token/network activity remains behind the same login calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One authentication flow per newly opened/reopened conversation, plus one shared setup-session restoration after release/runtime restart. Offered service choices are bounded to the two supported services.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing _sessionRestoration Sequencer serializes shared setup restoration. Warm callers reuse _attempt.session. Conversation authentication proceeds independently after joining that restoration; the diff adds no parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ready context and live setup session are reused. After release, the existing restoration path recreates the setup session. No new positive/negative cache or retry policy is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for repository-visible call counts, cache ownership, and ordering. Native SDK/runtime internals are not included in the selected diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime/network operation duration and SDK-version-internal behavior cannot be determined from package-version changes alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. The targeted API migration preserves verification cardinality and launch critical-path placement.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shared predicate is called by mapSessionEvents during existing event passes. It now skips provisional root stream events as well as provisional whole-message/tool events; committed messages and subagent streams retain their existing handling.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted event count; the added checks are constant-time per event. Ephemeral stream-event availability in persisted history is runtime-dependent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous mapping; no new task, loop over messages per delta, or service request is introduced by the predicate.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No memoization invalidation or history-cache lifecycle is changed by the diff. Existing reconstruction callers/cache ownership remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the pure predicate and its mapping call sites; the dependency update does not expose native history-storage implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether any ephemeral stream events appear in actual persisted history is not established; either way the predicate adds no expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Inspected the complete 11-file inventory and every diff page, then completed the performance pass with caller, timing-state, cancellation/reuse, phase-chat persistence, action-routing, account-launch, and history-mapper traces. Submitted one high-confidence medium-severity retained-output finding. No concrete performance-fix provenance signal was established. Review is static; native SDK/runtime implementation changes are opaque beyond the shown API/version migration.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
